results.title: Michael R. Young, The Past and Future in Hans-Georg Gadamer's Philosophical Hermeneutics
results.snippet: Gadamer not only asserts that history or tradition conditions understanding, but in "an ontological turn" he also makes the case that language is the foundation of philosophical hermeneutics.
extra_snippets: Hans-Georg Gadamer's philosophical hermeneutics seeks to provide an analysis of understanding expressed particularly in Truth and Method and in some of his later works. His goal is to describe "what is the case" in human understanding aside from and prior to any methodology. Gadamer's essential insight is his notion of historically effected consciousness .

Such a consciousness is a consciousness at once effected by history whether conscious or not of these effects. Gadamer not only asserts that history or tradition conditions understanding, but in "an ontological turn" he also makes the case that language is the foundation of philosophical hermeneutics.

His claim that "being that can be understood is language" moves him to conclude that philosophical hermeneutics is universally applicable in all understanding whatsoever. ;Gadamer's assertion of the universality of hermeneutics raises the specter of epistemological relativism by considering all understanding as historically, linguistically, and thus interpretively formed.

The is a brief study of Hans-Georg Gadamer's philosophical hermeneutics.

Since the publication of Martin Heidegger's Sein und Zeitin 1927, the hermeneutics are distinguished between traditional or methodological and radical or ontological hermeneutics. Based on early Heidergger's work, Gadamer interprets comprehension in ontological terms as one of the components of Dasein. It traces back to Plato's dialogue, and applies Hegel's dialectics. Further, Gadamer develops his philosophical hermeneutics, which has a tremendous impact on contemporary philosophy and literature.

Thus, hermeneutics is concerned not with the justification of interpretive understanding as knowledge or science, but rather it deals with different matters altogether ...
